title: Grill Mat Hacks for Making Homemade Jerky on a Gas Grill
meta_description: Discover how to use a grill mat for homemade jerky on a gas grill—step‑by‑step tips, seasoning tricks, and why BBQ Grill Mats are a game‑changer.
html:
Making homemade jerky on a gas grill is surprisingly easy when you use a grill mat. The homemade jerky grill mat creates a flat, non‑stick surface that prevents flare‑ups and lets the meat dry evenly without sticking. Below are the exact steps, tools, and seasoning hacks I rely on every time I fire up the grill.

Why a Grill Mat Beats a Traditional Grill Rack for Jerky

Grilling jerky on a typical rack leaves gaps where heat escapes, causing uneven drying and occasional burns. A grill mat offers:

  • Uniform heat distribution across the entire surface.
  • Zero sticking—no need for oil or spray.
  • Protection from direct flame, which eliminates flare‑ups.
  • Easy cleanup—just wipe or rinse the mat after use.

The BBQ Grill Mats are reusable, dishwasher‑safe, and sized to fit most standard gas grills, making them perfect for batch‑style jerky production.

Preparing the Meat: Trim, Slice, and Marinate

Start with a lean cut such as top round, eye of round, or turkey breast. Trim off any visible fat, then slice the meat against the grain into 1/8‑inch strips. For consistent thickness, freeze the meat for 30‑45 minutes before slicing.

Marinade is the flavor engine. A basic mix includes soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and a pinch of black pepper. Combine the ingredients, submerge the strips, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours—or overnight for deeper flavor.

Setting Up Your Gas Grill with a Grill Mat

1. Preheat the grill on low heat (around 150‑170°F). The goal is a gentle drying environment, not a sear.
2. Place the BBQ Grill Mats directly on the grill grates. Let the mat heat for a minute so it adheres lightly to the grill.

Because the mat is non‑stick, you can spread the meat strips side‑by‑side without crowding. This maximizes airflow, which is essential for that classic jerky texture.

Cooking the Jerky: Low‑and‑Slow Technique

Lay the marinated strips on the mat, leaving a small gap between each piece. Close the lid and maintain a steady temperature of 150‑170°F. Check the grill every 30 minutes and rotate the mat if your grill has hot spots.

Jerky is done when it is darkened, dry to the touch, and bends without breaking. This usually takes 3‑4 hours, but thinner strips may finish sooner. Resist the urge to crank up the heat; high temperatures cause the exterior to burn while the interior stays moist.

Finishing Touches and Storage

Once the jerky reaches the perfect chew, remove the mat and let the pieces cool on a wire rack. Pat any excess moisture with a paper towel. Store in an airtight container or zip‑lock bag; for longer shelf life, add a food‑grade desiccant packet.

Because the BBQ Grill Mats are reusable, simply wash them with warm soapy water or toss them in the dishwasher. They’ll be ready for your next jerky batch—or any delicate grilling project.

FAQ

Can I use a grill mat on a charcoal grill?

Yes. The mat works on any grill type—gas, charcoal, or even electric—provided the temperature stays within the recommended range for jerky.

Do I need to oil the grill mat before laying down the meat?

No. The non‑stick surface of the BBQ Grill Mats eliminates the need for oil, which keeps the jerky from becoming greasy.

How many times can I reuse the grill mat?

When cared for properly, the mat can be reused dozens of times. It’s designed to withstand high heat and frequent cleaning without degrading.
